newsitem.title: ITALY: Dornbusch attacks Italy over debt and EMU.
newsitem.headline: Dornbusch attacks Italy over debt and EMU.

text.p: U.S.-based economist Rudiger Dornbusch on Friday poured cold water on Italy's hopes of being a founder member of the European single currency.

In reply to a question about current Italian political problems with the government narrowly averting a crisis, he said "there will be a crisis here when (Helmut) Kohl has to exclude Italy from European Monetary Union in order to win elections (next year for chancellor)."
The Massachusetts Institute of Techology (MIT) professor was speaking at a conference on employment organised by the Italian employers' organisation Confindustria.
"Italy's problem isn't Maastricht, its problem is that the government is too indebted to sustain a far too high quality of life," he said.

Italy had erred by being too generous, indiscriminately handing out huge loans in favour of the private sector which helped to create "instability and an untenable public debt situation." It was time to put an end to this, he said.
"Italy seems to want to put off any serious reforms, borrowing from its citizens and hoping for a miracle. "But I don't believe there will be a miracle," Dornbusch said.
